title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6.0%)
drivers.evidence: Past 6% price increase (2026-09-28) had no promo and sold 13 units (vs baseline 10.2), but next week (2026-10-05) with same price sold only 3 units. This suggests demand drop at higher price. Noise-adjusted effect of price increase is estimated at -25%.

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no events, but a price increase to $4.08 (+6.0% vs $3.85). Past promotions show a median lift of x2.15, but noise-adjusted lift is x1.45. The 2026-09-07 Labor Day promotion (10% off) lifted sales to x1.75, and the 2026-09-28 week (same price, no promo) sold 13 units, near baseline. The 2026-10-05 week (same price, no promo) sold only 3 units, suggesting price sensitivity. The noise-adjusted effect of a 6% price increase is likely negative. Given limited evidence (only one past price change at this level), shrink toward 1.0. No event or promotion is scheduled. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends.

brief:
PRODUCT: Candy Corn Bag | category Candy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 25.3 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
